title: Nonvanishing Zhu C2 images of singular vectors in noncritical universal affine vertex algebras of complex simple Lie algebras
source_title: Simplicity of vacuum modules and associated varieties
author: Tomoyuki Arakawa; Cuipo Jiang; Anne Moreau
difficulty_reason: The nonvanishing of the Zhu image is not a formal consequence of the associated graded invariant ring, whose singular arc-polynomials can have positive depth. The author combines the commutative highest-weight reduction with a carefully chosen PBW monomial and an explicit Sugawara commutator expansion that controls its root and Cartan factors. The noncritical-level coefficient then rules out the proposed leading-term cancellation and forces zero depth, which is the nonroutine obligation behind the selected singular-vector statement.

Lemma3.4 explicitly says “Since the proof is similar to that of Lemma3.3, we left the verification to the reader”: bounded ancillary PBW verification using the supplied identical Sugawara operator and fully worked commutator expansion3.3; no independent new construction or omitted global core. Lemma3.2(a)–(c) “easy to see” likewise bounded finite PBW reorder checks. Printed Lemma3.6 opening (wi)^(0)=1 is an obvious superscript slip for the already-defined absence of the negative-root factor (wi)^(-)=1; its displayed remaining Cartan factor and subsequent proof explicitly retain (wi)^(0). No critical-level, Lie-superalgebra, or arbitrary singular arc-polynomial extension asserted.
